items.title: Interview: Graeme Jones
items.text: Graeme, thank you for joining us two years on from your arrival as sporting director. How do you chart the heart's journey from both a football and a performance perspective? Well, to answer it literally, when arrived two years ago, I think we were 10th in the table with nine points than during a difficult period. And as we sit here today following a turbulent few weeks, we are um fourth in the table with 20 points. So I think it's a sign of the ambition and standards that we now expect that we're disappointed with the last few weeks and the results and the injuries that have also come. Um, but that's also a sign of the progress that we've made that we are disappointed with where we're sitting just now. And I feel that last season, you know, it's important to acknowledge we were way ahead of um the schedule of where we would expect to be and we had outperformed what we would thought we were going to do and obviously ended very painfully in the end. So, it's perhaps um a little bit expected that we've got a period where we're, you know, rationalizing where we're at. Um but it's important to remember part of this journey of what we've gone through in the last 6 months. We've got a new head coach, a whole overhaul of players with some of our best players from last season departing. um new players coming in and adapting a new style of play and philosophy um and of course the the injuries as well. So um while it's been a difficult period for us, there's many things in this 2-year journey so far to remember and I do feel it's important that we just take note of of where we are um in this journey. Yeah, we we'll get straight into a hot topic at the moment relates to our injury list. As you you mentioned there, it seems unprecedented. Is it is it just bad luck or or from your point of view, is there there something that you've needed to to investigate further? Well, injuries are part of football. We all know this. um at a certain level with injuries, then as a sporting director, I need to look beyond the bad luck theory um and and dig into possible circumstances or or reasons as to why we find ourselves why where we are. You can read pretty much anywhere just now. Um, I read something this week about the English Premier League and the injury crisis they have and the year and year increase that they have in injuries particularly coming out of international duty. So, we're not unique in the position that we find ourselves, but there are a number of factors that I need to consider and acknowledge as to why we find ourselves where we are. So, we've got a new head coach that's brought in a an intended new front foot style philosophy of how we play. We have new players who are adapting to a more competitive league than what they've been used to previously. Um, we have European football which is becoming the the standard we want every season, but the demands that Thursday, Sunday brings on the team. And then there's also the part of the bad luck which is we've suffered a huge amount of contact injury so far this season more in this short period than the whole of last season. So unfortunate as although it is it's a convergence of all these factors um that has brought us to where we're at just now where we're missing a starting 11 of of of players. Um, but I also think it's important to realize that this this is there is light at the end of the tunnel. We have players returning for the game coming up on Saturday. We're hoping to have, you know, up to six, maybe even seven players possibly back into contention for first team training. Whether they're included in the squad, it just might be too soon, but we'll we'll manage that accordingly. So, I can only see and sit in here and be confident that, you know, both literally and figuratively, things are going to improve in the the second half of the season. I've got no doubts on that. Um, and also to reassure fans that we're not sitting on our hands, we conducted a external re review of our performance area at the turn of this year. We um utilized a external consultant who's considered one of the top high performance practitioners in the country in in the UK and he conducted an in-depth review that came with a numerous amount of recommendations of things that we needed to improve. We've implemented all of these things. We have invested heavily in our medical department. Um, and even though it might not feel like it from the outside looking in, we are in a much better place to deal with this unprecedented level of injuries that we have than we would have been a year ago. So, I appreciate that it is um will create dismay amongst a lot of our fans and the the wider public about how many injuries we've got. And of course, it's naturally impacted on a number of things, but it it would be far easier if it was one simple part of the system that was failing when unfortunately it's a convergence of all these factors. But we are coming out of it now, I believe, and we can have a little bit of optimism as opposed to the the pessimism that we've all been feeling lately. aligned with with the injuries in in many ways really. How would you assess the the first team's current form? You described it as a turbulent week. Few weeks. Yeah. Uh it's not been good enough. And um some of the manner of the defeats and some of the or the quantity of goals that we've conceded, it's just not been good enough. And I know that. Reuter knows that. The players know that. Um, and we're doing everything during this international week to recalibrate and rest and and put things put things right as best we can. Um, I talked earlier about where we were in the league two years ago. Um, because it's important to have the big picture in mind when you're in my role and and looking towards the future. But I totally understand. um the the shortterm results has a massive effect on the general harmony across the board particularly with our fans. So, and I would I would never sit here and tell fans to be patient and calm um during these periods. I am a fan. I've sat in a stand during some of the most worst times throughout the club's history. So I do understand but we as a club and me as a sporting director have to remain focused on the objectives and the the long-term future of the club and the success of the club that we are striving for. And I have to understand and we as a club have to understand there are going to be short-term trials and tribulations that we go through that are going to be disappointing at that moment in time that we have to come through. And I'm confident that we are coming through this. And I'm confident that we will have better resilience as individuals, as a team enable to enable us to to achieve the success that we're striving for going forward. So while it's been difficult, I'm confident that we will come through this much stronger as a collective after what was a a significant overhaul of of players in the summer. You mentioned earlier some of the guys that have departed the club obviously numerous new arrivals in the summer. How do you feel a lot of those guys have have settled into life at heart medium? Well firstly they are all individuals and like all individuals they all adapt differently. So there has been some real success stories with the players we've signed in the summer and that have contributed significantly to some of the successes that we have had this season so far. And then there's been other players that are still adapting and it would be much easier for players for me and also for the fans to everybody to come in to hit the ground running and to show their quality from the minute they step on the park. But unfortunately it doesn't work like that. And we can see in Scottish Premiership the nature of what Scottish football is, the intensity, the frantic nature of it, the ultra um ex, you know, the extra scrutiny that you get as a player in this league, the fan expectations that come with it, and just the general culture and environment is quite hostile for any player to come in and adapt to. um we're not in a unique position. There are high more high-profile players with much higher transfer values of players that have come this summer that are also taking time to adapt to the league. So in my role as sport director, I need to just focus on ensuring that these individuals are supported. Um for many of them, they're coming to a new country, a new language, a new culture. There needs to be an adaptation for them, for the language. their ability to become happy. It might involve their family settling and schooling. It can be just general relocation. So the infrastructure that we have around the players is very important and we've spent a lot of time and effort in the last two years improving this and it's in a much better place than it ever was. But all I can do is is ensure that we give the full round support of these players as we can and hopefully they adapt as quickly as possible. But as we've seen already from some of the players that have been successful this season. These players have taken six to 12 months in some cases to settle into life and in in hearts and Scottish football. But we believe in the model that we are part of. We believe in the players that we are recruiting and we trust our process completely and it's up to me and our staff to help support the players. So we have a collective responsibility in in achieving the success together. Staying with new arrivals, the January transfer window is just around the corner. What does that look like for us as a club? So we've obviously you've got to factor in the injuries part here. We've got a very large squad um with you know an double figures number of players that are unavailable recently. So as they return back we will naturally have to look at creating balance within the squad. So we will look to um decrease the size of the squad but also only add with quality. So it will be an active window like all transfer windows are but as we all know January is notoriously difficult. We've got plenty of evidence in the last two years that the players that have signed in January don't always come in and hit the ground running. So we we have to focus our attentions on the quality that can make a difference. Um but we will be very much looking to create a bit of balance within the squad once all our players come back are fit and available and then looking to add quality and also help people move on that aren't getting the opportunities. Staying with recruitment, Lee Wallace, he recently joined the the first team coaching staff. Can you give us some insight into into that decision and and what is the process for identifying his replacement in the the transition phase? Coach Ro. Well, he's got a long affiliation with the club, which is um very helpful and important um for for the culture within the club. He in my two years has shown to be a outstanding young coach. He's developed from being involved with the under 19s to this the start of this season as the trans transition phase coach which is a vitally important part of our pathway. um excelled in that area and because of the nature of European football and the success that we've had in qualifying for the group stages and also the injuries that we've sustained Lee became a much more pivotal part in the day-to-day next to the the first team coaches and Welter and the coaches came and asked if Lee could be part of the coaching setup because of the quality that he brings but also the the the benefit that it will bring to the the first team to have an extra coach to be able to work with players on a daily basis, but also the team when the the team travels abroad and Lee has a pivotal pivotal role in maintaining the the day-to-day training of the players that don't travel for the for the European games. So, he's been a fantastic addition. Um the fact that he's been a hearts player and has that hearts affiliation is an added bonus and I'm really excited to see his progress in the coming years and in relation to his replacement. We are active in that just now. Shelley K and Andrew Webster are leading on that and we will hope to have a new transition phase coach appointed by by the end of the year. There's a lot of focus at the moment on developing young players and and proposals by the governing bodies to to do so for the benefit of Scottish football. Can you tell us how that relates to our own academy and and where our own player development currently sits? Yes, the Scottish FA brought out um their proposals in early September as to what they want to move the game towards which I think is a positive step positive step and more young Scottish players playing in first teams is naturally a a positive step forward. We have a really clear um framework and pathway for our players through the Heartsway um headed up by Shelley K and supported by Andrew in the academy and it's vitally important to the the development of our young players. We have the challenge, like all Scottish clubs have the challenge of um our most talented young players at the point of signing professional contracts being um targeted by clubs down down south in England. On a financial level, we cannot compete just like none of the other clubs in Scotland can compete um with with these clubs. So what we have to do is provide a really really clear pathway that and means that the the bright lights and the the the increase in in in finances down south aren't as attractive and I believe that we've got that with with our hearts way already. This season we see the benefit of our transition phase group. In previous seasons, we've had a B squad, which was an extra squad, number of players, but not necessarily all players that we would be considered to be in the pathway to our first team. So, the transition phase has allowed us to take from our 19s and that area between the most talented players that we can focus our attentions on and utilize the club cooperation agreements and also the loan system. So all these players are getting first team minutes within the professional leagues. We get the benefit of being able to um look at these players also through Jamestown. But most specifically these players get to adapt to first team environment while also being under the cher of our coaches. We've also got a new initiative that's we're starting at the beginning of the year where we'll have three club mentors who are all ex players for hearts um that will act as the mentors to these young players in a transition phase that will help support all their off off pitch um development and complementing what a transition phase coach does. So the round care that we give and the clear pathway that we provide I feel is is is best in practice for for what we're looking to do. And I believe that that will be shown in in the course of time with the players that we we develop and bring through towards a first team like the James Wilsons and also now recently like Matty Gillis who's taken a difficult circumstance with the squad and injuries and and made it to the benefit of themselves off the back of you know a few thousand minutes playing first team football in the Championship and then the leagues below. So all in all the proposals are a positive step forward, but we are very very uh keen to commit to what what we are doing and and and the pathway that we've got in place. I'll go with the women's team currently as well. They currently sit second in the the SWPL. Obviously a big summer for them that's that's just gone by as well. How happy have you been with with their new signings and their new head coach in in Andy Thompson? Yeah, there's there's a lot of similarities between the women's team and the men's team because there was a real transform transformational year last year and far exceeded expectations the the achievements that the the women's team had and then to go through the overhaul of a new head coach, a whole new squad, um a new style of play, the similarities are there. Andy's been fantastic since he's come in. He's managed to maneuver a really difficult European schedule um and be very competitive throughout or unlucky to to to be knocked out to a very good team in Soiad. We're very competitive in the league. Slight gap appearing at the top, but that's okay. Um it was similar to that in previous seasons as well. So, we're in a really good space and Andy's really um picked up the batting very well and has brought the team together, has got them playing a really really positive front foot style of play. And again, there's a lot to be really optimistic about there on the journey that we're at with our our women's team. Just finally then, Graeme, we were under no illusions as to how challenging the domestic and and European schedule was going to be at the beginning of this season, but as we prepare to enter an even busier period up until Christmas, what would be your overall message to the the supporters of Hartman? Listen, we we have a as a football department, we have a collective responsibility with through myself, writers, the coaches, all the players to ensure that our commitment to improving us as a team and also our own field performances are there all the time, both through good moments and also through more challenging moments like we've been experiencing. But our commitment, our ef effort, and our resolve must be a given. And I can assure you they are. And I would reassure fans that these short-term results, while disappointing, will be just short-term. And as we look forward to the future with an improvement in our squad, with players returning and a strengthening across the board, our resolve will be better. And as a result, we will get back to playing at the level that we all know that we're capable of. So I do look forward to the coming difficult period of games with anticipation of success rather than fear of failure. Great. Thanks very much for Thank you very much.
